title: Touch move, draws, resigning, notation, the clock

card.idea: Some rules are not about the board at all. They are about how players behave: what happens when you touch a piece, how a game is written down, how it can end by agreement, and what the clock does to all of it.

explain.text: Touch move: touch one of your pieces and you must move it if it has a legal move. Let go of it on a square and it stays there. Say "I adjust" first if you only want to straighten a piece up.
Moves are written short. A letter for the piece and the square it goes to: Nf3. Pawns get no letter, so e4 is a pawn move. An x means a capture, + means check, O-O is castling short and O-O-O long.

Either player may offer a draw, and the other may accept or play on. A player who knows the game is lost may resign. With a clock, each player has a set time for all their moves, and running out usually loses the game.

challenges.prompt: The scoresheet says Nf3. Tap the square the knight is going to.

hints.text: The letter names the piece, the rest names the square.

challenges.reason: N is the knight, f3 is where it lands.

challenges.prompt: Both rooks can reach e1, so the scoresheet says Rae1. Tap the rook that moves.

hints.text: The extra letter tells you which file the moving rook starts on.

challenges.reason: When two pieces could go to the same square, the writer adds the file of the one that does.

challenges.prompt: White wrote O-O. Tap the two squares his king and rook finish on.

hints.text: O-O is the short side, the side the king has less ground to cover.

challenges.reason: O-O is castling on the king's own side: king to g1, rook to f1.

challenges.prompt: You pick up your knight, then spot a much better rook move. What does touch move say?
options: Play a knight move if the knight has one
Play the rook move, nothing has been said yet
Neither piece may move this turn
challenges.reason: Touched means moved. It is worth a habit of deciding first and reaching second.

challenges.prompt: Your opponent offers you a draw. What are you allowed to do?
options: Accept it, or turn it down and play on
Accept it, because an offer cannot be refused
Ignore it, an offer is not part of the game
challenges.reason: An offer is a question, not an order. Making your move is a polite no.

challenges.prompt: Your clock runs out while your opponent still has enough material to mate. What is the result?
options: You lose the game on time
You keep playing without the clock
challenges.reason: Time is part of the game: your thinking has to fit inside it.

challenges.prompt: White's next move on the scoresheet is O-O. Play it on the board.

wrong.Kf1: That is written Kf1. O-O moves the rook as well.
wrong.Rf1: That is written Rf1. The king has to travel too.

challenges.reason: O-O is the short castle, and here it is also the move that saves White from mate on f2.

challenges.prompt: White's next move on the scoresheet is O-O-O. Play it on the board.

wrong.Kd1: One O too few. Kd1 leaves the rook in the corner.
wrong.Rd1: That is written Rd1. O-O-O takes the king to c1 as well.

challenges.reason: The extra O is the longer journey: king to c1, rook to d1.

takeaway: Touch it and you move it, write your moves short, and watch the clock.
